rule.title: Important Windows Service Terminated With Error
rule.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)

es.summary: El Service Control Manager registró el evento 7023: un servicio de seguridad o de registro (Defender, firewall, EDR, BitLocker, EFS o Windows Event Log) terminó con error. Puede ser una falla legítima o un intento de deshabilitar las defensas.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos 7023 del log System (Provider_Name 'Service Control Manager') cuyo param1, es decir el nombre visible del servicio, contiene Antivirus, Firewall, Microsoft Defender, Threat Protection, BitLocker, Encrypting File System o Windows Event Log. También se detectan cuando el campo Binary contiene en hex UTF-16 el nombre interno: WinDefend, EventLog, mpssvc, Sense, EFS o BDESVC.
es.why_it_matters: Los atacantes detienen o provocan la caída de antivirus, EDR, firewall o del registro de eventos para operar sin ser detectados (ATT&CK T1562, Impair Defenses). La referencia de la regla es la guía de Microsoft para investigar el bootkit BlackLotus, que menciona que se deshabilita Microsoft Defender.
triage_steps: Identifique el servicio afectado: lea param1 y, si param1 está en otro idioma, decodifique Binary (hex UTF-16) para obtener el nombre interno.
Revise param2 (el código de error) y verifique si el servicio volvió a iniciarse (evento 7036 'running') o si sigue detenido.
En el mismo host, dentro de +/- 15 minutos, busque los eventos 7034, 7036, 7040 (cambio del tipo de inicio) y 7045 (servicio nuevo) del Service Control Manager.
Busque la creación de procesos (4688 o Sysmon 1) con sc.exe stop/config, net stop, taskkill, Set-MpPreference o herramientas desconocidas que apunten al servicio.
Si se trata de Windows Event Log, revise si hay huecos en los logs o eventos 1102/104 de borrado; si se trata de Defender, revise los eventos 5001, 5010 y 5012 del log operativo de Defender.
Verifique qué cuentas iniciaron sesión en ese momento (4624 o 4672) y si hubo alertas previas para el host o el usuario.
Compruebe si coincidió con un parche, una actualización de definiciones, un reinicio o un cambio de producto de seguridad.
false_positives: Caídas reales por errores del servicio, corrupción de archivos o falta de recursos; como dice la regla, el servicio puede terminar por muchas razones.
Actualizaciones de Windows, de la plataforma Defender o del agente EDR que reinician el servicio de forma brusca.
Cambio o desinstalación autorizada de un antivirus o firewall de terceros.
El patrón hex corto de EFS puede coincidir con otros servicios cuyo nombre interno contenga 'EFS'.
response_steps: Confirme con el equipo de TI o el dueño del endpoint si había mantenimiento planificado antes de tomar acciones.
Si no hay una explicación legítima, aísle el host con el EDR o restrinja su red, y conserve la evidencia (logs y memoria).
Restablezca el servicio y su tipo de inicio, reactive las protecciones y verifique que la telemetría llegue al SIEM.
Busque persistencia y alteraciones (servicios nuevos, claves de registro de Defender, exclusiones) y elimínelas tras validarlas.
Si se confirma el compromiso, restablezca las credenciales usadas y revise otros hosts en busca del mismo patrón.
es.severity_rationale: El nivel high es adecuado porque el servicio caído es un control de seguridad o de registro, y su pérdida reduce la visibilidad aunque la causa pueda ser benigna.

en.summary: Service Control Manager logged event 7023: a security or logging service (Defender, firewall, EDR, BitLocker, EFS or Windows Event Log) terminated with an error. It may be a real fault or an attempt to impair defenses.
en.what_it_detects: System log event 7023 from Provider_Name 'Service Control Manager' where param1 (the service display name) contains Antivirus, Firewall, Microsoft Defender, Threat Protection, BitLocker, Encrypting File System or Windows Event Log. It also matches when Binary holds the UTF-16 hex of the internal service name: WinDefend, EventLog, mpssvc, Sense, EFS or BDESVC.
en.why_it_matters: Attackers stop or crash antivirus, EDR, firewall or event logging so they can work without being detected (ATT&CK T1562, Impair Defenses). The rule's reference is Microsoft's BlackLotus bootkit investigation guidance, which mentions Microsoft Defender being disabled.
triage_steps: Identify the service from param1. If param1 is in another language, decode Binary (UTF-16 hex) to get the internal name.
Check the error code in param2. Then check whether the service restarted (event 7036 'running') or is still stopped.
On the same host within +/- 15 minutes, look for Service Control Manager events 7034, 7036, 7040 (start type changed) and 7045 (new service).
Look at process creation (4688 or Sysmon 1) for sc.exe stop/config, net stop, taskkill, Set-MpPreference or unknown tools that target the service.
For Event Log, check for gaps or 1102/104 log-clear events. For Defender, check events 5001, 5010 and 5012 in the Defender operational log.
Check which accounts were logged on at the time (4624 or 4672) and look for earlier alerts on this host or user.
Check whether the event lined up with patching, a definition update, a reboot or a security product change.
false_positives: Real crashes from service bugs, corrupted files or low resources. As the rule notes, a service can terminate for many reasons.
Windows, Defender platform or EDR agent updates that restart the service abruptly.
An authorized replacement or uninstall of a third-party antivirus or firewall.
The short EFS hex pattern may match other services whose internal name contains 'EFS'.
response_steps: Before acting, check with IT or the endpoint owner whether maintenance was planned.
If there is no legitimate explanation, isolate the host through EDR or restrict its network access, and keep the logs and memory as evidence.
Restore the service and its start type, turn protections back on, and confirm that telemetry reaches the SIEM again.
Hunt for persistence and tampering (new services, Defender registry keys, exclusions). Remove what you find once it is confirmed malicious.
If compromise is confirmed, reset the credentials that were used and check other hosts for the same pattern.
en.severity_rationale: High fits because the failed service is a security or logging control, and losing it reduces visibility even when the cause turns out to be benign.

positive.description: Microsoft Defender Antivirus service terminated with an error. The English display name matches 'Microsoft Defender' and ' Antivirus', and Binary contains the windefend hex.

event.param2: The system cannot find the file specified.

positive.description: German-language host: the display name does not match, but Binary contains the UTF-16 hex for EventLog.

negative.description: Print Spooler terminated with an error (7023). Neither the service name nor the Binary value is on the watch list.

event.param2: The service has returned a service-specific error code.

negative.description: Defender service state-change event 7036 (entered the stopped state) is not a 7023 termination with error.
